audit_scope.description: Trust boundary analysis for Ethereum protocol specifications covering P2P networking (eth/66, eth/64), EVM execution (contract creation, EOA delegation), and governance processes

misclassified_entities.reason: This is an internal component of the local node initiating P2P protocol requests, not an external entity crossing the trust boundary
This represents a contract executing within the EVM, which is internal to the Ethereum system. It does not cross the external trust boundary

trusted_external_entities.name: Remote Peer Node (P2P Network)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Remote Ethereum nodes in the P2P network are untrusted. They can send malicious or malformed protocol messages (Status, requests, responses) to attempt DoS attacks, provide incorrect chain data, or exploit protocol vulnerabilities. Validation of forkid, request_id correlation, and message structure is critical.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Sender (EOA via JSON-RPC)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External accounts submitting transactions via JSON-RPC are untrusted. They can submit malicious contract creation transactions attempting to exploit address collision vulnerabilities (EIP-7610) or manipulate gas usage. All transactions must undergo full validation including nonce, signature, gas limits, and EVM execution constraints.

trusted_external_entities.name: Type-4 Transaction Submitter (EIP-7702 Authorization)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users submitting EIP-7702 type-4 transactions with authorization tuples are untrusted. They can attempt replay attacks, submit invalid authorization signatures, or delegate EOAs to malicious contracts. Nonce-based replay protection, signature validation (EIP-2 low-s check, ecrecover with MAGIC prefix), chain_id verification, and authorization list validation are mandatory.

trusted_external_entities.name: External Caller to Delegated EOA
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: EVM CALL/STATICCALL/DELEGATECALL opcodes targeting delegated EOAs
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External contracts or EOAs calling delegated accounts (EIP-7702) are untrusted. They can attempt to exploit storage collisions, bypass tx.origin checks in non-topmost frames, or trigger unexpected delegation resolution behavior. Proper storage namespacing (ERC-7201) and gas accounting (cold/warm access costs) must be enforced.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Attacker
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Multiple vectors: JSON-RPC, P2P network, EVM execution
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Adversaries actively attempt to exploit protocol vulnerabilities including authorization replay (EIP-7702), residual storage address exploitation (EIP-7610), P2P DoS via fork incompatibility claims (EIP-2364), and request_id correlation attacks (EIP-2481). All protocol layers must implement defense-in-depth with validation, rate limiting, and cryptographic protections.

trusted_external_entities.name: EIP Proposal Author
trusted_external_entities.rationale: EIP authors are external to the protocol implementation. They can propose changes affecting consensus, networking, or API layers. Proposals must undergo community review, security analysis, and formal approval before implementation. Incorrect layer classification (EIP-4) could cause improper stakeholder review, missing critical security implications.

trusted_external_entities.name: Core Client Developers
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Client implementation and consensus rule changes
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Core developers implement protocol changes and maintain client software. While they have elevated trust due to reputation and multi-party review processes, they are still external to the running protocol. Bugs or malicious implementations can cause consensus failures, network partitioning (EIP-4), or security vulnerabilities. Formal specification review and multi-client implementation diversity provide defense.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Request messages with request_id must be validated for RLP structure, 64-bit request_id format (P type), and bounded tracking state to prevent memory exhaustion. Response correlation relies on request_id matching without content inspection (EIP-2481).

ForkID validation (EIP-2364) must detect incompatible chain configurations via forkHash (CRC32 of genesis + fork blocks) and forkNext comparison. Malicious peers lying about fork configuration must be disconnected immediately to prevent chain synchronization attacks or eclipse attacks.

Contract creation transactions must validate that target addresses have zero nonce, zero code length, AND empty storage (EIP-7610). Non-empty storage check prevents code injection into 28 known mainnet addresses with residual storage from pre-EIP-161 behavior, maintaining code immutability guarantee.

Type-4 transactions must validate: (1) non-empty authorization list, (2) non-null destination, (3) sender is EOA or has delegation indicator, (4) sender nonce incremented BEFORE authorization processing. Authorization tuple validation: chain_id match, nonce < 2^64-1, ecrecover with MAGIC prefix, s <= secp256k1n/2 (EIP-2), authority code state check, nonce match. Nonce-based replay protection prevents reuse of signed authorizations.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: EVM CALL/DELEGATECALL opcodes with delegation indicator detection
boundary_edges.security_assumption: When code starts with 0xef0100 delegation indicator (EIP-7702), must extract 20-byte target address and verify it is NOT a precompile (execute empty code if precompile). Delegation resolution incurs COLD_ACCOUNT_READ_COST (2600) or WARM_STORAGE_READ_COST (100). Delegation loops only follow first level. Storage collision risk mitigated by delegate contracts using ERC-7201 namespaced storage.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Multiple: JSON-RPC (transaction replay), P2P (forged messages), EVM (delegation exploits)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Defense-in-depth required: (1) Nonce incrementation prevents authorization replay (EIP-7702), (2) Storage check blocks residual address exploitation (EIP-7610), (3) ForkID validation prevents fork-based eclipse attacks (EIP-2364), (4) Request_id tracking prevents response misrouting (EIP-2481). All external inputs undergo cryptographic validation (signatures, hashes) and structural validation (RLP, bounds checks).

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: EIP governance process and layer classification
boundary_edges.security_assumption: EIP classification (EIP-4) determines review stakeholders. Consensus layer EIPs can cause network partitioning if implemented inconsistently. Authors must correctly identify affected layers; incorrect classification leads to inadequate security review. Multi-stakeholder review and formal specification are required before consensus changes.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Client software implementation of consensus rules
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Implementation bugs or disagreements on consensus layer changes cause network partitioning (EIP-4). Multi-client diversity and formal specification reduce risk. All clients must converge on identical consensus rules for cryptographic commitments and settlement. Testing on testnets before mainnet activation is critical.

coverage_analysis.notes: All truly external entities have been mapped to boundary edges. Two entities (EXT-CLIENT-INITIATOR, EXT-CALLING-CONTRACT) were correctly identified as misclassified internal components. Governance entities (EIP authors, core developers) are included as they influence protocol behavior through the EIP process and implementation, representing trust boundaries in the protocol evolution process.
